candidates.attribution: Florida’s county property appraisers, Florida Department of Revenue Property Tax Oversight
candidates.description: The Florida Department of Revenue’s Property Tax Oversight(PTO) program collects parcel level Geographic Information System (GIS) data files every April from all of Florida’s 67 county property appraisers’ offices. This GIS data was exported from these file submissions in August 2026. The GIS parcel polygon features have been joined with the real property roll (Name – Address – Legal, or NAL) file. No line work was adjusted between county boundaries.The polygon data set represents the information property appraisers gathered from the legal description on deeds, lot layout of recorded plats, declaration of condominium documents, recorded and unrecorded surveys. Individual parcel data is updated continually by each county property appraiser as needed. The GIS linework and related attributions for the statewide parcel map are updated annually by the Department every August.  Minor data maintenance is also completed every May and November. The dataset extends countywide and is attribute by Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) code. DOR reference with FIPS county codes and attribution definitions - https://fgio.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=55e830fd6c8948baae1601fbfc33a3b2 If you discover the inadvertent release of a confidential record exempt from disclosure pursuant to Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, public records laws, immediately notify the Department of Revenue at 850-717-6570 and your local Florida Property Appraisers’ Office.   Please contact the county property appraiser with any parcel specific questions: Florida Property Appraisers’ Offices: Alachua County Property Appraiser – https://www.acpafl.org/ Baker County Property Appraiser – https://www.bakerpa.com/ Bay County Property Appraiser – https://baypa.net/ Bradford County Property Apprais

candidates.description: These boundaries are of cities and villages within the state of Ohio. No determinations have been made as to the types of municipalities for each entity. Municipality is a broad term for an area that has its own local government. In Ohio, a municipality is any incorporated local government which has its own charter or was created under state law. Ohio municipalities are classified as either: Cities (population ≥ 5,000) Villages (population < 5,000) In Ohio, "municipality" is either a city or a village. This data was derived from County Parcel data and ODOT Municipality data by combining the Parcel and ODOT municipalities, then removing any parcels that were designated as not municipality. Any slivers or artifacts created in error were removed. It was then edge matched to appropriate boundary datasets then dissolved to create one feature for each municipality. Feature Service updated on 5/6/2025 with 119 annexations throughout the state. These annexations were as of 1/30/2025. Updates will be ongoing. Feature Service updated on 6/23/2025 to include U.S. Census decennial population estimates for 2000. 2010, 2020 and population estimates for 2024. Feature Service updated on 1/1/2026 to add sq miles to cities. Feature Service updated 4/27/2026 to include 139 recent annexations, as of January 2026.

candidates.description: Overview This feature service supports a parcel adjustment project for the Sandy Springs area using parcel and subdivision reference layers. It brings together parcel polygons, parcel boundary and centerline support features, parcel identification and annotation content, and subdivision records used to maintain corrected parcel geometry and associated reference information. Feature Layers Adjusted Parcels provides parcel polygons with ownership, assessment, address, land use, subdivision, and update information used to support corrected parcel records. Parcel Lines and Soft Lines contain parcel boundary linework and curve-related attributes that help represent adjusted parcel geometry. Centerlines provides a minimal line layer used as part of the parcel adjustment dataset structure. PIN stores parcel identification features and related parcel reference details such as acreage, plat, deed, and recording information. Subdivisions contains subdivision names and plat references that support parcel indexing and adjustment workflows. Annotation Points stores text annotation elements used to place labels and parcel-related annotation content. Geographic Coverage The service covers a local parcel adjustment area for Sandy Springs in Fulton County, Georgia. Use Cases Maintaining corrected parcel boundaries and related parcel reference layers Supporting parcel review and update workflows from recorded plats and surveys Displaying parcel identifiers, subdivision references, and label placement for cartographic products Providing local parcel editing support for GIS applications and web mapping Data Stewardship Recorded plats and surveys are incorporated into the adjustment workflow on a recurring basis. Fulton County remains the authoritative source for parcel data.

candidates.title: Current Parcels
candidates.description: Parcel data from Fulton County for the most recent tax year. This layer can be used in software programs and apps so only the data layer needs to be updated instead of each individual program or app. Fulton Update Date attribute is the Last Updated Date from the Fulton County GIS Open Data site. From Fulton: This dataset represents the boundary of each parcel of land in Fulton County recorded for the purpose of aiding in the appraisal of real property and the determination of property tax. A parcel dataset is created each year in association with that year's tax digest. The parcel dataset for any given year is not considered final until the completion of the digest, which generally occurs around mid-year. Until the completion of the digest, the parcel dataset is considered to be a work in progress. Any necessary corrections and omissions may continue to be made even after the completion of the digest. The parcel dataset in its published form incorporates information from the CAMA (computer-aided mass appraisal) database. The CAMA information included with the published dataset is selected based on its value to the typical consumer of the data and includes the parcel identification number, the property address, property owner, owner's mailing address, tax district, assessed and appraised value for land and improvements, the number of livable units, acreage, property class and land use class.

candidates.description: This dataset represents tax parcel boundaries within Wayne County, Pennsylvania. Parcels are maintained for property assessment, taxation, and general mapping purposes. In addition to parcel geometry, this dataset contains selected Computer-Assisted Mass Appraisal (CAMA) information, which may include owner name, mailing address, parcel identification number, and other assessment-related attributes. This information is part of the public record in Pennsylvania and is provided here for informational purposes. Parcel boundaries are compiled from recorded subdivision plans, deeds, and other official documents. While every effort is made to ensure accuracy, parcel geometry and attribute information may not reflect the most current recorded documents or on-the-ground conditions. Assessment and ownership information is provided for informational purposes only and may not reflect recent transfers or changes. For official ownership records, legal descriptions, or recorded documents, consult the Wayne County Assessment Office and the Recorder of Deeds. This dataset is not a legal survey, deed, or title document and should not be used for legal determinations, property transfers, or boundary disputes. Data is updated periodically as changes occur through subdivision, consolidation, transfer, or correction processes.

candidates.description: This polygon feature class represents the boundaries of historical land warrants in Wayne County, Pennsylvania, digitized from original warrant maps held by or referenced through the Pennsylvania State Archives and related repositories. The majority of warrants date to the colonial and early national period (pre-1800), with some extending into the early nineteenth century. Each polygon reflects the surveyed lot lines of individual land warrants as depicted on the source maps, which were georeferenced to modern spatial reference systems prior to digitization. Attributes include warrant owner names, warrant numbers, acreage, survey dates, and township/range designations. This dataset is intended to support historical land research, genealogical inquiry, and planning analysis within Wayne County. Source materials were georeferenced from original warrant maps. Boundary accuracy is dependent on the precision and condition of the source cartographic documents. Users should be aware that warrant boundaries may not align precisely with modern parcel boundaries or legal survey records. Warrants located near municipal boundaries may appear compressed or stretched as a result of geometric inconsistencies introduced when fitting adjacent maps together during georeferencing. This dataset is intended for historical research and planning reference purposes only and should not be used for legal boundary determinations. Gaps and overlaps present are intentional as a means to remain as accurate as possible. Lineage Source materials were obtained from the Pennsylvania State Archives, Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (PHMC). Specifically, the maps are from RG-17 Records of the Land Office — Warrantee Township Maps, Series #17.522, available online at: https://www.phmc.state.pa
